name: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muʾmin ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaḍramī al-Ishbīlī
summary: Al-Shalawbīn's student and the last great grammarian of al-Andalus, author of al-Muqarrab on naḥw and al-Mumtiʿ on ṣarf.
bio: Ibn ʿUṣfūr was born in Seville in 597/1200 and studied with al-Shalawbīn for some ten years. He taught in the cities of al-Andalus as they fell one by one to Castile, and then in Tunis at the court of the Ḥafṣids, where he died in 669/1270; the reports of his end differ, and some tie it to his losing the ruler's favour.

His al-Muqarrab gives the whole of naḥw in clear, numbered divisions and was much studied; his al-Mumtiʿ fī al-taṣrīf is one of the fullest books on ṣarf, with the changes of the weak letters, ibdāl and idghām set out case by case. He wrote three commentaries on al-Zajjājī's al-Jumal and a book on the licences of the poets (Ḍarāʾir al-shiʿr). Abū Ḥayyān, a generation later, quotes him constantly.

sources.title: İbn Usfûr el-İşbîlî, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
